asset_label: building seen from a post-disaster aerial (UAV) image
source_note: FEMA Preliminary Damage Assessment classes (FEMA PDA Guide, July 2025) as documented in docs/research/03_competitors_underwater_industrial_disaster.md and 05_damage_grading_standards.md. Descriptors are paraphrases aligned with CAL FIRE DINS percent-damage bands (Affected 1 to 9 percent, Minor 10 to 25, Major 26 to 50, Destroyed over 50) and the xBD Joint Damage Scale. Replace with verbatim FEMA matrix text before customer use.

rows.criterion: No visible damage to roof, walls or surroundings.
Cosmetic damage only: some shingles or siding missing, debris on the property, building habitable; roughly 1 to 9 percent of the structure affected.
Nonstructural damage such as partial roof covering loss, broken windows or doors, minor water intrusion; repairable and habitable after repair; roughly 10 to 25 percent.
Structural damage: roof decking or wall sections gone, partial collapse, building not safe to occupy until repaired; roughly 26 to 50 percent.
Total loss or damage so extensive that repair is not feasible: collapse, only foundation or debris field remaining; more than 50 percent.
Structure cannot be assessed from the image (obscured by water, smoke, trees, cloud or outside the frame).

unified_note: Mid-scale classes (Minor versus Major) are the hardest to separate from imagery; when torn between two adjacent classes, choose the lower one and lower confidence rather than escalate on guesswork, except where collapse is visible.

flags.not_measurable: set when the percent-damage estimate cannot be made
